---
title: "Planned Training and Software Increments"
---

The current course stops after a Redis Lists transport, transactional MongoDB
outbox, and durable MongoDB projection archive. The next two increments will
coexist with that implementation so learners can compare transport and replay
models on the same business flow.

## Module 14: Redis Streams in parallel

### Software increment

- Add stream keys that do not replace the existing Lists keys.
- Publish the same versioned event contract to both paths behind explicit configuration.
- Add one consumer group per logical service.
- Expose pending entries, acknowledgements, retry, and reclaim behavior.
- Add end-to-end tests that compare duplicate delivery and recovery.
- Keep the Angular extension contract unchanged.

### Training outcomes

Learners will explain consumer groups, pending entries, acknowledgements,
retention, ordering, and replay. The lab will stop consumers, inspect the
pending-entry list, reclaim a message, and compare the result with `LMOVE`.

### Entry criteria

- The Lists path remains green in CI.
- Both paths use the same `AuctionWon` contract version.
- Metrics make delivery and acknowledgement visible.

## Module 15: Retained-log CQRS operations

### Software increment

- Introduce an explicit command endpoint and write model.
- Version and replace the existing rental summary projection.
- Add lag metrics and operational replay controls.
- Display retained-log checkpoints in Angular diagnostics.
- Support idempotent rebuild from a retained event source.
- Test lag, replay, schema evolution, and projection replacement.

### Training outcomes

Learners will distinguish CQRS from Event Sourcing, design an idempotent
projection, reason about stale reads, and rebuild a read model without changing
the write model.

### Entry criteria

- The current Lists transport and Mongo archive reconstruction runbook are understood.
- Event ordering and versioning policies are documented.
- The user interface can display eventual consistency explicitly.

## Deliberate exclusions

Kafka, full Event Sourcing, and distributed transactions are comparison topics,
not implementation requirements for these two increments.
